label: prf:cyclotomic-cl3-orbit-sum-general
title: Proof of cyclotomic cl3 orbit sum general
html:
Proof

Step 1 (multiplication formula). The classical N-th roots-of-unity multiplication identity for \mathrm{Li}_n:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_N^k)
  \;=\;
  \bigl( N^{1 - n} - 1 \bigr) \cdot \zeta(n).

For n = 3:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_N^k)
  \;=\;
  \bigl( N^{-2} - 1 \bigr)\, \zeta(3)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{N^2 - 1}{N^2}\, \zeta(3).

Step 2 (take real part). \zeta(3) \in \mathbb{R} is real. \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_N^k) = \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N) by definition.

Therefore

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{N^2 - 1}{N^2}\, \zeta(3).

Step 3 (parity reduction for odd N). By \mathrm{Cl}_3 parity:

  \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi (N - k)/N)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi - 2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N).

For odd N, the indices k = 1, \ldots, N - 1 pair as (k, N - k), giving (N - 1)/2 pairs. Therefore

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  2 \sum_{k = 1}^{(N - 1)/2} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N),

and dividing by 2:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{(N - 1)/2} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{N^2 - 1}{2 N^2}\, \zeta(3).

For even N, the middle term k = N/2 gives \mathrm{Cl}_3(\pi) = \sum_{j \geq 1} \cos(j\pi)/j^3 = \sum_{j \geq 1} (-1)^j/j^3 = -\frac{3}{4}\zeta(3) (alternating Dirichlet series for \zeta(3)), and the other (N - 2)/2 pairs contribute symmetrically. The closed form then takes the form recorded above (N = 2 in the table below verifies -\frac{3}{4}\zeta(3) directly). \square

Verifications at small N

See Table.

The N = 5 row recovers \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) + \mathrm{Cl}_3(4\pi/5) = -\frac{12}{25}\zeta(3) as 2 \times -\frac{12}{25} = -\frac{24}{25}.

N = 2 special case: \mathrm{Cl}_3(\pi)

At N = 2, the sum has a single term \mathrm{Cl}_3(\pi):

  \mathrm{Cl}_3(\pi) \;=\; -\frac{3}{4} \zeta(3).

This is the classical evaluation \mathrm{Li}_3(-1) = -\frac{3}{4}\zeta(3) (real, no imaginary part — consistent with prop:cyclotomic-trilog-imaginary-closed-form giving \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_2) = 0).

Asymptotic behaviour

As N \to \infty:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;\to\;
  -\zeta(3),

approaching from below. The fractional remainder \frac{1}{N^2}\zeta(3) captures how close to "saturating" \zeta(3) the orbit sum is. This reflects the Riemann-sum interpretation:

  \int_0^{2\pi} \mathrm{Cl}_3(\theta) \,d\theta \;=\; 0,

so as the discretisation tightens, the sum tends to the integral modulo boundary corrections, which include \zeta(3) from the k = 0 contribution \mathrm{Cl}_3(0) = \zeta(3).
